_comment_enabled: Set to true to make this rule active. Keep false while using this file only as documentation.
_comment_main_priority: Chooses which matching rule wins. Higher values are selected before lower values.

match._comment_type: Matches every item whose Epic Fight weapon capability type is this value.
match._comment_item: Use item instead of type to match one exact item id, for example "epicfight:uchigatana". Do not define both item and type.

_comment_match: match must contain exactly one of type or item.

animations._comment_priority: Chooses which animation entry is tried first inside this rule. Higher values are tried first.
animations._comment_style: Optional. This entry only applies when the current Epic Fight style name is SHEATH.
animations._comment_run: FastRun animation id to play for this entry. If it cannot be resolved, the next matching entry is tried.
animations._comment_left_step: Optional. Left-foot step animation id. If one step is defined, both left_step and right_step must be defined.
animations._comment_right_step: Optional. Right-foot step animation id. If both step animations resolve, manual/startup steps can use them.

animations._comment_priority: This entry demonstrates matching more than one style with styles.
animations._comment_styles: Optional alternative to style. Use this when the same animation should apply to several Epic Fight style names.
animations._comment_run: A run-only entry uses this animation and lets the mod create procedural step pulses.

animations._comment_priority: This entry demonstrates the built-in WOM weapon sprint family.
animations._comment_run: When WOM is installed, this resolves to the WOM weapon sprint animation family. Without WOM, it is skipped.

animations._comment_priority: This entry demonstrates a style-specific Epic Fight run animation as a fallback candidate.
animations._comment_style: Only used while the weapon is in SHEATH style.
animations._comment_run: Uses Epic Fight's normal sheath run as the source. No-WOM FastRun can procedurally pulse a run-only entry.

animations._comment_priority: Lowest priority catch-all entry for styles not handled above.
animations._comment_run: No style restriction means this entry can match any current style if higher priority entries do not apply.

_comment_animations: Entries are sorted by priority. style/styles only filter an entry; they do not change the rule match target.

effects._comment_startup_step: When true, FastRun may trigger a step pulse when the sprint animation starts.
effects._comment_manual_step: When true, manual FastRun step input is allowed if the selected profile has step animations or a custom run animation for procedural pulse.

_comment_effects: Step effects no longer require WOM Natural Sprinter. With WOM Natural Sprinter available, WOM step resource is consumed; otherwise the generic FastRun step cooldown config is used.

run_pose._comment_enabled: When true, applies the FastRun run-pose adjustment while this profile is active.
run_pose._comment_scale: Strength of the run-pose adjustment. 0 disables movement; larger values make the pose stronger.
run_pose._comment_blend_ticks: How many ticks the run-pose adjustment takes to blend in or out.

_comment_run_pose: Controls only the extra FastRun pose layer, not which animation id is selected.

step_pose._comment_scale: Strength of the procedural step pose pulse. 1.0 matches the built-in default, 0.5 is half strength, and 0 disables only the pose offsets.
step_pose._comment_duration_ticks: How many ticks the procedural step pose pulse lasts. 10.0 matches the built-in default.
step_pose._comment_forward_impulse: Horizontal forward velocity added when a procedural step fires. 0.8 matches the built-in default, and 0 disables the extra push.

_comment_step_pose: Controls only procedural FastRun step pulses. Real left_step/right_step animations keep using their authored animation, though their visual/audio effects still follow the selected profile.
_comment_fallback: Used when no animation entry can be used. weapon means use the current weapon run as the procedural FastRun source; barehand means use the barehand fallback family.
